## Work Experience

**Bioinformatics Research Assistant (**Aug. 2023 – Present)

*Department of Bioinformatics and Computational Biology, University of North Carolina, Charlotte, North Carolina*

-   Building a pipeline for structural variant genotyping using pangenome graphs, integrating tools like Vgtool kit, Minimap2, Cactus, etc.

-   Employed statistical and machine learning methods such as Wald’s test, hypergeometric test, PCA to uncover novel genetic elements and the molecular mechanisms underlying biological processes. Some of these biological processes were the therapeutic effects of drugs and stress effects.

-   Utilized computational tools to construct a pan-transcriptome that helped uncover 70% more differentially expressed genes compared to when the conventional pipeline that involves a single reference genome was used.

-   Developed a pipeline for bulk-RNA seq analysis with a pan-transcriptome as the reference sequence and processed datasets of over 8 TB in size.

-   Employed R (tidyverse, UpSetR, DESeq2, glmmSeq, clusterProfiler) and Python (pandas, subprocess, concurrent, bs4, requests, matplotlib) packages for data processing and visualization.

-   Expedited the execution of computational-intensive tasks (e.g., genome indexing, alignment) by utilizing HPC environments, optimizing time-consuming tasks through parallel processing.

-   Developed a workflow and documentation for the easy utilization of a legacy bioinformatic tool, reducing setup and execution time by 50%.

**Research Assistant (**Feb. 2022 – Jul. 2023)

*Institute of Plant Breeding, Genetics & Genomics, University of Georgia, Georgia*

-   Leveraged basic and advanced QTL mapping techniques in R to analyze large peanut datasets, leading to the discovery of novel loci associated with yield and supporting the Georgia peanut breeding program.

-   Performed statistical analysis of peanut phenotypic data in R, employing ANOVA and correlation tests to derive insights.
